Date: 2025-03-05
Start: 15:00 PT

Attendees: Alex Martin, Samira Khan (Redwood); Priya Patel, Tom Garcia, Luca Rossi, Maya Chen (DataRiver)
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on onboarding progress, access setup and env readiness. Discussed S3 access, VPC peering, test tokens, KMS integration, and next steps for benchmarking and security docs. Action items assigned for access and benchmarking setup.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martin: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to do a quick weekly sync on the POC onboarding and make sure envs are green.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Yeah thanks Alex, we got most of the infra spun up but we're still waiting on the access bits from you for the test tokens.
[00:20] Samira Khan: Quick note, we already generated a short-lived test token earlier but I'm not sure if you got the email, I'll re-share after the call.
[00:28] Tom Garcia: We didn't see it, might've been blocked by our spam. Also for the VPC peering we need your CIDR and the peer AWS account id.
[00:38] Alex Martin: Perfect, we'll drop the account id in the slack thread and Samira will upload the runbook.
[00:45] Luca Rossi: From security perspective we need to confirm KMS integration, are you supporting customer-managed KMS or is it Redwood-managed?
[00:52] Samira Khan: For the hosted POC we can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping — there are two options: bring-your-own KMS with an IAM role we can assume, or use Redwood-managed with envelope encryption. We can send both flow diagrams.
[01:06] Maya Chen: Is there any on-prem option for the dataset? We want to avoid copying larger than 50GB out of our environment.
[01:12] Samira Khan: For that you'd look at Redwood Private or a connector that mounts S3 via a private link; we also support streaming from S3 to the model without a full copy. It's not the on-prem box but it's private networked.
[01:25] Priya Patel: Great. For the benchmark — what's the plan? Are we running the default script or do you recommend customizing prompts?
[01:32] Samira Khan: We'll provide a benchmarking harness that uses your prompt set and a sample config. The harness supports different models and batching configs. It'll emit latency and p99 numbers and token cost.
[01:45] Tom Garcia: We want to validate both Hosted API and Dedicated pool performance, is that feasible in the POC?
[01:52] Alex Martin: Yes, we can run both. For Dedicated we need reserved capacity — we can spin up a short-term dedicated pool for the benchmark window to get apples-to-apples throughput.
[02:05] Priya Patel: Do you have any baseline numbers against similar workloads?
[02:10] Samira Khan: We have an internal perf sheet, but baseline depends on sequence length and batch sizes. We'll share an example table — tends to be lower latency on dedicated for steady throughput.
[02:22] Priya Patel: Makes sense. On the access front, I tried to create the service principal but ran into permission errors uploading the dataset.
[02:29] Alex Martin: Tom, can you confirm the IAM policy you used? We typically ask for s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket scoped to the test prefix and ability to create a role for KMS decrypt if you're using CMK.
[02:41] Tom Garcia: I used an admin-ish role but the bucket policy also denies cross-account unless we add the Redwood account. I'll patch that today.
[02:49] Luca Rossi: Also need to confirm retention — are logs retained in your control plane? We need audit logs for the POC.
[02:58] Samira Khan: Yes, by default we retain audit logs for 30 days on hosted. For Dedicated/Private we can configure retention longer; we'll include the retention table.
[03:10] Priya Patel: Ok thanks. About benchmarks — if we run the throughput test, what's the recommended request rate?
[03:18] Samira Khan: Start small: steady ramp to your expected QPS, use our harness with ramping steps every minute, measure token-per-second and p99 latency. We'll help tune batch sizes and model variants.
[03:32] Alex Martin: To finalize scheduling, what's the earliest you can provision the test dataset and VPC details?
[03:38] Tom Garcia: I can share VPC peering details by Monday; I'll open the ticket after this call.
[03:44] Priya Patel: I can upload the sample dataset by Monday as well, path will be s3://dr-poc-test/requests.jsonl
[03:50] Maya Chen: One more note, our compliance team asked about SSO — do you support SAML SSO for the console and audit trails?
[03:58] Samira Khan: Yes, we support SSO via SAML/Okta, and you can set up SCIM provisioning; we'll send the SSO configuration doc.
[04:08] Alex Martin: We'll also send the SOC2 package and the KMS integration notes after the meeting.
[04:14] Priya Patel: Thanks. On the test tokens, can we get a token with reduced permissions for the harness?
[04:20] Samira Khan: Yep we can provision a token scoped to read-only inference endpoints and revoke it after tests.
[04:27] Tom Garcia: About cost — how will you measure token cost for the benchmark? We want a per-1M token estimate for each model variant.
[04:36] Samira Khan: The harness will log tokens consumed and we'll attach the cost model sheet — that gives you an approximate unit cost. For Dedicated we can show committed discount scenarios.
[04:48] Priya Patel: Any blockers from Redwood side for running the Dedicated short-run?
[04:53] Alex Martin: No blockers — we just need a booked window and confirmation of approximate QPS and model choice.
[05:00] Luca Rossi: On encryption: if we use customer-managed KMS, can Redwood access the plaintext in the control plane? We need to be sure keys are never exported.
[05:08] Samira Khan: With BYO KMS we only use keys for envelope encryption and don't export keys; we'll add the detailed crypto flow to the security doc.
[05:18] Priya Patel: Ok thanks. Any other integration notes — like network egress or private link?
[05:23] Samira Khan: We support VPC peering and private link. For large datasets we recommend S3 private link to avoid public egress.
[05:30] Alex Martin: Quick recap then: Redwood will share the runbook, benchmarking harness, SOC2 + KMS notes by next week; DataRiver will share VPC peering info and upload dataset by Monday. Samira will coordinate the benchmarking window.
[05:46] Priya Patel: That matches my notes.
[05:50] Tom Garcia: I'll create the support ticket now.
[05:53] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, that's helpful.
[05:57] Alex Martin: Thanks all, we'll follow up in the slack thread with the artifacts and proposed benchmark times.
[06:03] Priya Patel: Great, bye.
[06:05] (call ends)
